candidates.label: Metastatic neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid) of mediastinum, stage IV with bone metastases (T1, T2), hypocalcemia, complicated by acute respiratory failure and cardiac arrest

response.rationale: The large mediastinal mass with lytic vertebral lesions in a young woman, treated with dexamethasone, strongly suggests an aggressive lymphoma (PMBCL) with bone metastases. Acute respiratory failure and PEA arrest likely from mass effect. Low calcium is atypical but may be secondary to hypoalbuminemia or renal dysfunction; hypertension may be stress-related. Thymic carcinoma is less likely given age and sex. Other candidates are less supported by the overall picture.
